title: Life-stack manifest
description: A machine-readable description of a personal health-measurement instrument: what it measures, how each source is ingested, what protocols and supplements are under measurement, and what it costs to own. Deliberately describes the INSTRUMENT and never the subject — no health metrics, no per-day records, no lab values, no identifiers. Published so the architecture can be forked without the data. Reference implementation: https://averagejoematt.com/data/stack.json

generated_by.description: The generator that produced this file. A manifest a human edits by hand is a manifest that drifts; state the generator so a consumer knows the file is derived.

schema_version.description: Semver of this schema. Minor = additive fields; major = a field changed meaning or was removed.

updated.description: UTC date the manifest was last regenerated.

architecture.description: The shape of the pipeline in vendor-neutral terms. Intentionally carries no resource names, account identifiers, ARNs, bucket names or function names — a fork should copy the shape, not the deployment.

services.description: Generic service categories, not product names.

ingest_patterns.description: The distinct ingest patterns present in sources[]. Derived, not declared.

key_choices.description: The decisions a fork would most regret getting wrong.

sources.description: Every data source the instrument publicly advertises. A source that exists but is not yet publicly advertised is absent by design.

category.description: Public grouping, e.g. Wearables / Inputs / Manual logs / Clinical / Archive.

measures.description: What this source measures, in reader-facing words.

method.description: How the data arrives, including cadence.

posture.description: The value verdict. load-bearing = something depends on it; portfolio = kept for breadth; paused = deliberately off; archive = frozen, no writer.

behavioral.description: True when a record exists only because a human DID something (weighed in, trained, logged). A gap is then a logging lapse, not a broken pipe — so it must never page anyone. False = infrastructure: the pipe runs unattended, and a gap means something broke. This one boolean is the most portable idea in the manifest; getting it wrong is how an operator learns to ignore alarms.

paused.description: Deliberately not ingesting. Never counted as stale.

raw_scheme.description: The SHAPE of this source's immutable raw archive — never a concrete key or bucket. Present only for sources that keep a raw archive.

device.description: The consumer product behind the source, where one exists.

purchasable.description: False = in the pipeline but not something a reader can buy (a free API, a hand-logged signal, a bridge over another source).

protocols.description: The interventions held under continuous measurement — their DEFINITIONS only. Results (findings, adherence, signal strength) belong to the subject and are deliberately excluded from this manifest.

tier.description: foundation / intervention / measurement / supporting — how load-bearing the protocol is.

definition.description: What the protocol IS — the rule being followed.

mechanism.description: The claimed physiological mechanism. A claim, not a result.

tracked_by.description: Which sources hold this protocol accountable.

supplements.description: The supplement stack at exactly the granularity the public catalogue already renders — name, group, dose, timing, evidence grade, monthly cost, paused. No wider.

grade.description: The catalogue's own evidence grade. 'emerging' explicitly means the human evidence is thin — it is published rather than hidden so a reader can discount it.

confidence_pct.description: The catalogue's confidence figure for that grade. A judgment, not a meta-analysis.

cost_monthly_usd.description: Typical retail spend per month. An estimate, not a receipt.

paused.description: In the catalogue but not currently taken. Kept visible rather than deleted so the record of what was tried survives.

cost_of_ownership.description: What it costs to run this instrument. Every figure carries a `basis` (how it was derived) and a `confidence`. Where no honest source exists the value is null with a basis explaining why — a null here is a deliberate claim that the number is unknown, not a missing field.

monthly_usd_typical.description: The trailing run-rate as published on the instrument's own live cost page. Read from the same constant that page reads, so the two cannot disagree.

ceiling_usd.description: The self-imposed hard monthly limit, enforced in code.

surge_ceiling_usd.description: The limit the ceiling floats to while real reader traffic exceeds the trigger below.

composition.description: The bill decomposed into its fixed and variable halves.

actuals.description: Complete billed months only. Partial and in-progress months are excluded: a partial month is not a run-rate.

live_endpoints.description: Where a reader can check the live bill rather than trust this file.

active_monthly_usd.description: Sum over the non-paused catalogue rows in this same file — a reader can add them up and get this number.

devices.description: Hardware and app-subscription cost. Null figures are deliberate.

time.description: Human time cost. Null figures are deliberate; the derived touchpoint counts are what can honestly be said instead.

recurring_manual_touchpoints.description: Counted from sources[] — the only two places recurring human action is structurally required.

ingestPattern.description: How a source's data arrives. A closed vocabulary — a source that matches none of these fails the manifest build rather than being silently filed as manual.

usdRange.description: An inclusive [low, high] USD range. A range rather than a point estimate wherever the underlying figure genuinely varies.
